walkthroughs.body_html:
Area of Study 2: Popular Song - Blues, Jazz, Swing and Big Band — a core area of A-Level Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area of Study 2: Popular Song - Blues, Jazz, Swing and Big Band brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area of Study 2: Popular Song - Blues, Jazz, Swing and Big Band.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Scat singing is best described as what?
options: Improvised vocals on nonsense syllables
Singing the melody an octave lower
Speaking the lyrics in rhythm
Humming the bass line

mcqs.q: Which instruments typically form the rhythm section of a swing big band?
options: Piano, guitar, double bass and drums
Three clarinets and a tuba
Violin, viola and cello
Two trumpets and a saxophone

mcqs.q: Blue notes most characteristically involve flattening which scale degrees?
options: The third, fifth and seventh
The first and the octave
The second and fourth only
The sixth only

mcqs.q: In swing style, pairs of written quavers are usually performed how?
options: Unequally, in a long-short pattern
Exactly as written, perfectly even
As triplet crotchets
Staccato and on the beat

mcqs.q: Is the blues always slow and sad?
options: Blues must always be played in a major key on a banjo.
Any slow, sad song counts as a blues, and all blues are slow and sad.
No - blues is defined by its form, harmony and blue notes; tempos and moods range from laments to up-tempo jump blues.
Big bands play entirely from memory with no arrangements at all.

mcqs.q: In a swing big band, does everyone improvise at once?
options: No - big band music is largely written in arrangements; improvisation is mostly given to featured soloists over the band's riffs.
Jazz means everyone makes it up together, so big bands improvise collectively all the time.
Blues must always be played in a major key on a banjo.
Big bands play entirely from memory with no arrangements at all.
Deliberate vocal improvisation using nonsense syllables, treating the voice like an instrumental soloist.
Scat is what happens when a singer forgets the words and covers it up.
Blues must always be played in a major key on a banjo.
Scat is singing the same lyric in several languages.

Improvised jazz singing on nonsense syllables, treating the voice as an instrument, made famous by Louis Armstrong and Ella Fitzgerald.
